drhp.business: International Conveyors Limited manufactures specialised PVC solid-woven conveyor belts used for continuous transportation of bulk materials in demanding operating environments, particularly underground mining, coal handling and mineral processing. It also runs a Treasury segment that deploys surplus funds in fixed-income and market-linked investments.
drhp.expansion: The Company has developed and launched a new product, Mineplast Pro (cover thickness up to 3 mm, DIN Abrasion of 150 mm3), aimed at competing with rubber/PVG belts. It has obtained various regulatory approvals for a superior low-abrasive, thicker-cover belt to penetrate a market currently dominated by PVG, with market entry expected from the second half of FY27 and trials already underway. No new plant, line or site commissioning timeline is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.note: Business is significantly dependent on mining and other core industries such as coal, cement, steel and power; any slowdown in mining activity, postponement of new projects, reduction in capital expenditure or adverse changes in commodity cycles may affect demand for Conveyor Belting.
risks.risk: Dependence on mining and core industries

risks.note: PVC resin, synthetic yarn, chemicals and other petroleum-based inputs are key raw materials; fluctuations in crude oil prices, raw-material availability, forex rates and supply-chain conditions may raise production costs and pressure margins.

Significant international market presence exposes the Company to geopolitical conditions, trade restrictions, tariffs, sanctions, political instability, economic slowdowns or regulatory changes in overseas markets that may adversely affect exports, customer demand and profitability.

International business exposes the Company to currency fluctuations; adverse movements against the Indian Rupee may affect export realisations, profitability and the value of foreign-currency-denominated assets and liabilities.

Large mining and industrial customers may account for a significant portion of demand; delays in project commissioning, changes in procurement policies, loss of major customers or sales concentration in particular markets may affect revenues and cash flows.

Conveyor belts for underground mining are subject to stringent safety, quality and certification requirements across jurisdictions; failure to obtain, renew or maintain required approvals could restrict access to certain markets.

Operations depend on timely availability of raw materials, transportation and logistics infrastructure; disruptions from geopolitical events, port congestion, freight-rate increases or natural disasters may affect production schedules and delivery commitments.

Customer expectations are shifting towards longer-life, energy-efficient and application-specific belts; failure to continuously improve products, manufacturing processes and technical capabilities may affect competitiveness.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Business is significantly dependent on mining and other core industries such as coal, cement, steel and power; any slowdown in mining activity, postponement of new projects, reduction in capital expenditure or adverse changes in commodity cycles may affect demand for Conveyor Belting.
- PVC resin, synthetic yarn, chemicals and other petroleum-based inputs are key raw materials; fluctuations in crude oil prices, raw-material availability, forex rates and supply-chain conditions may raise production costs and pressure margins.
- Significant international market presence exposes the Company to geopolitical conditions, trade restrictions, tariffs, sanctions, political instability, economic slowdowns or regulatory changes in overseas markets that may adversely affect exports, customer demand and profitability.
- International business exposes the Company to currency fluctuations; adverse movements against the Indian Rupee may affect export realisations, profitability and the value of foreign-currency-denominated assets and liabilities.
- Large mining and industrial customers may account for a significant portion of demand; delays in project commissioning, changes in procurement policies, loss of major customers or sales concentration in particular markets may affect revenues and cash flows.
- Conveyor belts for underground mining are subject to stringent safety, quality and certification requirements across jurisdictions; failure to obtain, renew or maintain required approvals could restrict access to certain markets.
- Operations depend on timely availability of raw materials, transportation and logistics infrastructure; disruptions from geopolitical events, port congestion, freight-rate increases or natural disasters may affect production schedules and delivery commitments.
- Customer expectations are shifting towards longer-life, energy-efficient and application-specific belts; failure to continuously improve products, manufacturing processes and technical capabilities may affect competitiveness.
